India and the United States continue negotiating a trade deal built on an interim agreement announced on February 7, 2026, while India prepares for its free trade agreement with the European Union. The commerce ministry said in a Saturday statement that the India-EU FTA is expected to come into effect in early 2027, following formal signing by mid-December during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Brussels visit and at least three-to-four months of post-signing operationalization. Commerce minister Piyush Goyal stated on Friday that the deal would take effect by March or April next year.

Under the India-EU agreement, duties will end upon entry into force for 70.4% of the EU's tariff lines, covering 90.7% of India's export value, with a further 20.3% of tariff lines being phased out over time. People close to development said, requesting anonymity, that India would sign the proposed interim bilateral trade agreement only after all tariff uncertainties are resolved, including responses to the United States Trade Representative's Section 301 investigation into excess capacity and product-specific Section 232 actions.

The USTR office proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods following an investigation into structural excess capacity in manufacturing. The rate would fall to 17% if India reaches an agreement, a point below the 18% agreed in February's interim framework and below rates proposed for export rivals such as Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand at 18%, plus Vietnam at 20%. Exporters have questioned how much that edge is worth.

The statement also described a sixth round of negotiations with Canada held from November 11-20, aimed at securing an agreement benefiting farmers, industries, businesses and MSMEs. Negotiations are underway with Chile, Peru, Israel, the Eurasian Economic Union, Mexico and other partners. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal addressed exporters during outreach initiatives in Jaipur and Dehradun on Friday.

The ministry cited Piyush Goyal's note that India's preferential access to global markets expanded from around USD 10 trillion in GDP a few years ago by an additional USD 60 trillion over four-and-a-half years, reaching approximately USD 70 trillion. The statement projected this could expand to around $85 trillion, representing nearly 76% of global GDP, over the next year and a half.
items.title: India Continues US Trade Talks While Targeting Early 2027 EU FTA Rollout

items.summary: On 25 November 2026, the US Office of Trade Representative released its Section 301 report on India under the US Trade Act of 1974. The document frames Indian manufacturing as suffering from structural excess capacity that justifies tariffs, yet it also acknowledges what Washington calls success in building production beyond market levels. It identifies Make in India, Production Linked Incentive schemes, and Atmanirbhar Bharat as the chief drivers behind this expansion.
items.title: Trump tariffs

items.summary:
The Telangana High Court has expressed serious reservations about the State Bank of India advancing a loan of nearly Rs 500 crore to M/s Sem India Fab Pvt Ltd for establishing a semiconductor manufacturing facility at Fab City near Hyderabad, even though the project had made no tangible progress. Justice Nagesh Bheempaka questioned why the bank sanctioned such a large loan when the company had failed to make substantial investments against a proposed total of around Rs 20,000 crore, observing that collateral or mortgage alone could not justify advancing an enormous sum without evidence of adequate assessment of repayment capacity.

The court suo motu impleaded the Central Bureau of Investigation in Hyderabad as a respondent and directed the Registry to provide it with case records. The dispute concerns 100 acres allotted under a February 16, 2006 memorandum of understanding for an ATMP semiconductor unit planned at roughly $2.25 billion; the government resumed 78 acres on February 9, 2010, while SBI claimed it advanced loans around Rs 500 crore based on NOCs and a mortgage created in August 2011.

The judge noted that the loan was sanctioned more than a year after land resumption began, that government NOCs did not transfer title since ownership remained with TGIIC, and that even by 2022 only an unfinished shed stood on the remaining 22 acres. The court found no material showing the company had invested as much as 50 or 75 per cent of its proposed cost before seeking the loan.

Emphasising established banking principles, the High Court observed that a borrower's sources of repayment should be primary rather than collateral alone, and noted neither SBI nor the company demonstrated adequate due diligence. The matter was posted to December 4, 2026.
items.title: Telangana HC questions SBI's Rs 500-cr bet on stalled semiconductor project

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday urged the Congress party to set aside political differences and support the government's Delimitation Bill, arguing that concerns raised by various states and communities had already been addressed. He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a proposal designed to take into account every state while ensuring 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies (ev1). Rijiju appealed to Congress members as well as those opposing the bill at their behest to join hands in Parliament, framing the measure as an effort toward women's empowerment. He said the proposed legislation would not only provide that 33% reservation but also increase the number of elected representatives in Parliament and state assemblies (ev2).

Rijiju accused Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge of opposing a democratic process, saying 'The Congress party has never believed in democracy' and questioning why they opposed a bill aimed at empowering women. He suggested that Rahul Gandhi may have influenced Kharge's position but added he could not say so with certainty (ev5). The Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday to implement one-third reservation for women across Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.

Rijiju noted that this proposed legislation differs from the earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, mainly in its approach to delimitation, the allocation of seats among states, and the census data used for redrawing constituencies.
items.title: Rijiju Urges Congress to Back Delimitation Bill

items.summary:
A compromise signed on October 12, 1968 was intended to settle a land dispute over the Katra Keshav Dev complex in Mathura, where the Lord Krishna Janmabhoomi temple and Shahi Eidgah mosque stand. The agreement laid down boundaries between the two structures, specified which portions each side would receive, and sought to prevent future disputes over access and construction.

Nearly 58 years later, Hindu litigants argue that the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh lacked authority to compromise property belonging to the deity. The Muslim side has relied on the agreement and civil court decrees from 1973 and 1974 to contend that the dispute was already settled.

On November 20, 2026, Justice Avnish Saxena of the Allahabad high court dismissed an application seeking a declaration that the October 12, 1968 agreement was null and void. The dismissal also sought cancellation of decrees passed in 1973 and 1974 and delivery of vacant possession to the deity.

The court held that this relief could not be decided through an interim application because it formed part of connected suits requiring a trial, so the order was made without affecting the merits of those cases. The next hearing is scheduled for December 10.

In its August 1, 2024 judgment, the Allahabad high court recorded the historical narrative advanced by Hindu plaintiffs and allowed their suits to proceed rather than dismissing them at threshold under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The court observed that questions about the legality and validity of the agreement were factual issues requiring evidence during trial.

The dispute concerns a 13.37-acre property, which Hindu plaintiffs claim was dedicated through a trust deed dated March 9, 1951 to the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust. The plaintiffs argue that this trust and the Seva Sangh were separate legal entities, with the latter neither owning the property nor having authority over it.

Advocate Kanu Agarwal told TOI that 'the deity or the trust were never the parties to Civil Suit No. 43 of 1967 or to the compromise deed dated 12.10.1968.' He described the Seva Sangh as a distinct legal entity from the Janmabhoomi Trust and stated that it 'prima facie was not the owner of the suit property.'

The plaintiffs further contend that neither the deity nor the trust was a party to Civil Suit No. 43 of 1967 or the subsequent settlement, arguing that the Seva Sangh conceded land it had no right to surrender.

Defendants have contested this position by noting that the compromise was entered into by recognised representatives with Waqf Board permission obtained through a letter dated September 9, 1968. The Muslim side has relied on subsequent civil court decrees and argued that a challenge cannot be brought through fresh proceedings.

The central legal question remains whether the Seva Sangh had authority to enter into the compromise, whether it could bind the deity and trust, and what effect should attach to the 1973 and 1974 decrees. The Allahabad high court has not delivered a final verdict on these matters.

The current litigation gained momentum in 2020 when advocate Ranjana Agnihotri and six others filed a suit seeking ownership of the property, removal of the Shahi Eidgah structure, and restoration of the temple. This raised broader debate around the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991.

Advocate Kanu Agarwal said 'the compromise deed of 1968 has no bearing or connection with [the] Places of Worship Act,' adding that the site's religious character and title would require detailed trial. In May 2022, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi questioned the revival of the dispute by tweeting that 'Sri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh and the Shahi Idgah Trust had resolved their issues by an agreement in 1968,' asking why it was being revived now.

The Hindu side maintained that the agreement was not binding on the deity and needed examination by a court. A survey of the disputed premises remains linked to Supreme Court proceedings, with Justice Avnish Saxena noting he could not pass a fresh order until the Supreme Court finally adjudicated the pending petition.
items.title: Allahabad High Court Defers on Validity of 1968 Mathura Compromise

items.summary:
Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) is preparing to release tickets for the special Vaikunta Dwara Darshan at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala, with the darshan facility set to run for 10 days from December 20 to 29. According to a Times of India report, TTD officials have finalized an online booking schedule across different categories of tickets and tokens so devotees can plan their pilgrimage.

The announced schedule lists Srivani Darshan tickets releasing first on November 28 at 10 am (ev1), followed by ₹300 Special Entry Darshan tickets on November 30. Online registration for Slotted Sarva Darshan tokens through the electronic dip system opens December 1 and closes December 5, with e-Dip allocation of those tokens scheduled for December 7.

In view of expected heavy crowds during the festival, TTD has decided to cancel VIP Break Darshan except for protocol dignitaries, along with ₹300 Special Entry Darshan tickets on December 20 and 21 (ev2). During these two days devotees can access darshan only through online e-Dip Slotted Sarva Darshan tokens. The decision aims to allow a larger number of ordinary devotees to participate in the special darshan during the peak festival period.

Separately, TTD sources say that after a Chennai-based couple donated gold ornaments to Lord Venkateswara, arrangements were made on Friday to adorn the deity with the newly donated jewellery. Donors Vardhaman Jain and Radhika Jain presented 46 different gold ornaments (ev3) weighing a total of 121 kg and valued at approximately ₹208 crore (ev5), which TTD sources describe as the largest offering ever made by an individual devotee to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala.
items.title: TTD to Release Vaikunta Dwara Darshan Tickets From November 28; Cancels VIP Break and Special Entry on Festival Days

items.summary: Lu You, a 12th-century Chinese poet, was among the first to explore the inner lives of cats. The item is presented as part of Eco India's Episode 340, which focuses on how citizens across cities are championing clean and accessible mobility.

items.summary:
Anusua Mukherjee, deputy editor of Frontline, reflects on the sesquicentenary of Rassundari Devi's Amar Jiban (My Life), which she notes is being reissued by Writers Workshop Kolkata in a new edition of Enakshi Chatterjee's 1999 translation. The memoir was published around 1876 and marks one of the earliest examples of women's writing in Bengali, written at age 88 by a woman born near 1809 who married at 12 and had 12 children, seven of whom survived.

Mukherjee observes that although Amar Jiban does not read as radical on its surface—its flat voice presents social conventions as endured realities rather than questioned ones—the text is more complex. She points to Rassundari's use of divine attribution for her desire to learn reading and specifically references the Chaitanya Bhagavata, noting that Jyotirindranath Tagore's introduction suggests this strategy successfully deflected criticism.

She connects the memoir to contemporary translation work through Bloomsbury's 5 Stories series, which includes anthologies of long short stories translated from Kannada, Konkani, Marathi, Sinhala, Malayalam, and Urdu. Mukherjee quotes reviewer Rohini Mokashi-Punekar as calling these stories 'surprisingly impactful and deeply affecting,' while noting that the conditions described in Amar Jiban persist 150 years later.

The piece closes with a personal anecdote about her grandmother's illiterate mother versus her literate, English-educated daughter. Mukherjee uses this contrast to argue that if patriarchy is timeless, so too is defiance.
items.title: Frontline marks 150 years since Rassundari Devi's Bengali autobiography

items.summary: Mini Krishnan serves as series editor for two anthologies collecting long short stories in Kannada and Konkani, offering introductions that frame translation as a means of cultural travel away from sterile homogenisation. The reviewer notes that all 10 stories employ realism while portraying non-elite characters whose lives are obscured by social position or gender (ev1). Susheela Punitha and Vidya Pai strengthen the realistic mode in their translations, often rendering spoken sociolects without italics to immerse readers in the original cultural worlds. The Kannada anthology contains five stories bookended by two women authors: Vaidehi's 'Worlds within Worlds' examines Brahminical patriarchy through a trapped bride and Dalit woman whose agency comes only through labour, while Banu Mushtaq's 'Not a Woman', rooted in the Bandaya movement, explores how class undermines religious precept (ev2). Other Kannada selections include Bolwar Kunhi's 'Worship,' Amaresh Nugadoni's tea-stall story set against Kargil and cricket that probes nationalism and religious polarisation, Mogalli Ganesh's Dalit-focused 'The Spinning Top,' plus works by Vaidehi and Banu Mushtaq. The anthology is published by Bloomsbury India at 200 pages for Rs.499 (ev3). Vidya Pai situates the Konkani stories within the language's recent literary emergence following its Sahitya Akademi recognition in 1975 and Eighth Schedule inclusion in 1992, featuring five writers from Goa including Jnanpith awardee Damodar Mauzo. The reviewed works include Mauzo's 'Cry Now' on Goan Catholic traditions, Pundalik Naik's 'Jait' about impoverished agricultural labourers, Jayanti Naik's and Mahabaleshwar Sail's laments for vanishing rural life, and Prakash S. Parienkar's experimental environmental story (dt4). The reviewer concludes that both anthologies chart little-known cultural terrains of India in original ways and recommends them highly; the author is Rohini Mokashi-Punekar, whose 2023 book on Mahatma Phule appears separately (dt5, dt6).
items.title: Anthologies of Kannada and Konkani Short Stories

items.summary:
The Economic Times explains systematic withdrawal plans (SWPs) as a method for retirees to generate regular income from a fixed savings corpus after they no longer have salary or other steady earnings. Under an SWP, an investor invests a lump sum in a mutual fund scheme and then withdraws a fixed amount at regular intervals.

Many mutual fund analysts believe that SWPs are more beneficial than dividends for obtaining regular money because equity-mutual-fund dividends depend on market movements and the profit earned by the fund house rather than being guaranteed. The publication notes that an SWP calculator shows the balance remaining after all withdrawals, requiring inputs such as total investment amount, monthly withdrawal needed, expected annual rate of return, and total investment horizon.

The article provides a step-by-step calculation using the PMT formula to determine the closing value or balance left after withdrawing amounts at regular intervals. The example instructs readers to enter their lumpsum investment amount, the desired monthly withdrawal, an assumed 12% rate of return (ev3), and a 10-year withdrawal horizon before entering opening balance, withdrawal amount, returns, and closing balance.

The piece carries a disclaimer that recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by experts are their own and do not represent the views of The Economic Times. Readers can submit mutual fund queries to ET Mutual Funds via Facebook/Twitter or email at ETMFqueries@timesinternet.in along with age, risk profile, and Twitter handle.
items.title: Systematic Withdrawal Plans Offer Regular Income From Mutual Funds

items.summary:
Speaking at CNBC Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh event, Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator is working on a proposal to create a separate trading platform for pre-IPO shares and that work was already underway. He added that a consultation paper would be released soon and framed the idea as one of several measures being examined amid significant expansion in India's IPO market over the past three to four years.

Pandey clarified that the proposed exchange would cover only companies preparing to launch an IPO, not the entire unlisted market, which he said comprises lakhs of companies. He emphasized that investor protection and safeguards would be central to designing the mechanism, including additional disclosure requirements, before a framework is finalized.

The announcement followed Sebi's November 23 advisory cautioning investors against grey market premium figures, which it described as unofficial, unverified and unregulated premiums circulated through websites, digital platforms and newspapers. The regulator also stated that these figures have no regulatory backing despite being presented as indicators of an IPO's expected listing price or potential returns.

Separately, Pandey said Sebi aims to reduce the time for foreign portfolio investors to complete onboarding from several months to as little as five business days, part of a broader review covering IPOs, corporate bonds and market technology. He also noted that Sebi proposed removing the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs to align India's rules with global standards.

At an ASSOCHAM conference in New Delhi, Pandey outlined four priorities: simplifying regulations, deepening markets to support economic growth, facilitating access for global investors, and expanding technology use while maintaining safeguards. He cited that India's equity market valuation crossed Rs 500 trillion, equivalent to more than 130% of GDP, and that companies raised around Rs 9 trillion through equity and debt markets in the first seven months of the financial year, including approximately Rs 1.45 trillion through 235 IPOs.

Pandey questioned whether a market twice its present size could remain fair, stable and trusted while serving a larger economy and financing more enterprises.
items.title: Sebi Considering Dedicated Exchange for Pre-IPO Shares

items.summary:
President Droupadi Murmu has recommended the Delimitation Second Bill 2026 for consideration by the Lok Sabha, following its approval by the Union Cabinet. The formal presidential sanction permits the bill's introduction during a special session of the Lok Sabha scheduled for November 30. That session is intended to gauge whether the National Democratic Alliance retains sufficient support and enough numbers to pass the legislation.

Bharat Rashtra Samithi has expressed backing for the delimitation bill, citing its role in securing southern parliamentary representation and strengthening treasury benches toward a majority in the Rajya Sabha. Separately, security measures were heightened at Tirupparankundram hill ahead of the Karthigai Deepam festival, with the deployment of CRPF and Rapid Action Force personnel.

Retired judges have been overseeing temple operations after the Supreme Court suspended the temple trust board, while authorities maintain a buffer zone and monitor the ceremony amid political and community responses. In other developments, Kolkata Police sealed the entrance to Trinamool Congress headquarters under construction over safety concerns and deployed additional forces, and Elementary Teacher Training teachers demonstrated in Chandigarh demanding full salaries and protesting corruption linked to job allocations.
items.title: President Murmu Forwards Delimitation Second Bill 2026 to Lok Sabha

items.summary:
Transport Minister C P John said on Saturday that the Kerala government plans to set up road safety councils at local body levels and promote grassroots road clubs as part of efforts to reduce accidents in the state. He described a two-pronged 'enlighten and enforce' approach under the Jeeva-Suyathra Mission, combining public education with strict enforcement against traffic rule violators.

John said accident-prone locations are now being identified using a grid system that divides the country into one-km-by-one-km squares, supported by around six to seven lakh volunteers from organisations including the National Cadet Corps and police cadets. He noted speed limits would continue varying by road type rather than undergo blanket revision, citing 70 kmph on a six-lane highway as an example.

On KSRTC operations during the Sabarimala pilgrimage season, John said 461 buses were operating exclusively for pilgrims and that 110 old damaged buses had been refurbished. He added MLAs had contributed 110 buses to support the corporation, with a mayor expected to provide one more.

John also addressed reports of cyber fraudsters using fake traffic challans, saying he had informed police to initiate legal action though incidents were not widespread. On delays in appointing board and corporation chairpersons, he said discussions within the UDF were underway and hoped the process would complete soon.
items.title: Kerala Transport Minister John Outlines Road Safety Councils

items.summary:
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam announced on Saturday that it would support the delimitation bill, which proposes increasing Lok Sabha seats in all states by 50 percent. The DMK passed this resolution at a meeting chaired by party chief MK Stalin, stating that the change 'will protect Tamil Nadu's representation.' Party leader A Raja said after the meeting that the party's consistent demand is that its seat share of 7.18 percent should not be altered, and he was quoted saying procedural issues would be addressed with an amendment if necessary.

The bill will be introduced by the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance government in Parliament during a special session beginning Monday, after the Union Cabinet cleared it on Friday. The legislation maintains the current proportion of seats based on the 1971 census and freezes the arrangement for another 25 years until 2051.

The DMK had previously opposed the bill while part of the Opposition INDIA bloc but is now supporting it, a shift that comes as its relationship with Congress has strained after Congress extended support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government in Tamil Nadu. The party still holds 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.

The bill requires a two-thirds majority of votes in Parliament to pass, which the ruling NDA does not have in either House, so it needs Opposition support. It had failed to secure that majority when introduced as the 2026 Constitution 131st Amendment Bill during an April special session. The Nationalist Congress Party faction led by Sharad Pawar also announced its support after the Cabinet cleared the bill on Friday; it has eight Lok Sabha MPs and one Rajya Sabha member, though it had voted against the bill in April.

The Opposition INDIA bloc contends that delimitation could upset the political balance between states and give BJP an electoral advantage through gerrymandering. A Raja noted that Stalin previously said there was no question of compromise on the exercise, even as the party raised concerns about its possible adverse effects.

items.summary:
The Supreme Court permitted a one-time ritual of lighting a ceremonial lamp at a disputed stone pillar on Thirupparankundram hill, but the November 20 order did not resolve the underlying religious and legal dispute over the pillar's identity, history, or access to the contested site near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. The BJP and Sangh Parivar have recast this limited interim measure as a broader Hindu triumph, with leaders describing it as 'the Ayodhya of the South' and Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoking Lord Murugan.

The Court's November 27 response to non-compliance by State and temple authorities escalated significantly: it directed that the lamp be lit on November 28, issued contempt notices to officials, suspended the temple board of trustees, appointed two former High Court judges as receivers, deployed CRPF personnel, permitted devotees to light lamps at least 50 metres from the Dargah (ev1), and vacated its earlier stay of relevant High Court findings. The article raises questions about whether such extensive intervention in a religious institution's administration was proportionate.

The BJP's Assembly strength reportedly fell from four MLAs to one in the 2026 election, yet the party frames the controversy as serving a national campaign ahead of northern State elections (dt2). The proximity of the Hindu temple and Muslim place of worship is presented as an opportunity for broader contestation over religious identity. The article also criticizes media language that describes the disputed structure simply as 'Deepathoon,' suggesting this risks settling its character in public perception before it is settled in law, while noting the Court referred to it only as a pillar identified as Deepathoon.

The piece concludes that when political mobilization, judicial intervention, and media language reinforce one another, an unproven claim can acquire the appearance of an established right. It argues disputes must be resolved based on evidence, law, and custom rather than political pressure, warning against using the lamp to mobilize one community against another.
items.title: Supreme Court's One-Time Lamp Order Recast as Hindu Political Victory

items.summary:
Security measures have been intensified at Tirupparankundram hill in preparation for the Karthigai Deepam ceremony, with CRPF and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed alongside additional troops to maintain order. Two retired judges are overseeing temple activities following the Supreme Court's suspension of the temple trust board, and contempt notices were issued to key officials due to non-compliance with judicial orders.

Devotees have participated in prayers and ceremonially lit the Deepam under strict supervision, while a buffer zone has been established around the nearby dargah. Political and community leaders have responded to the ruling, with continued dialogue ongoing on jurisdiction and religious concerns.
